claim_text: Among 341 patients with PIK3CA-mutated tumors, median progression-free survival was 11.0 months versus 5.7 months, with a hazard ratio of 0.65 and higher overall response in the alpelisib arm; most patients in the PIK3CA-mutated cohort were classified as endocrine resistant under protocol definitions `pmid-31091374`.
evidence_summary: SOLAR-1 randomized 341 patients with PIK3CA-mutated disease; alpelisib-fulvestrant improved median PFS to 11.0 vs 5.7 months with HR 0.65, increased overall response 26.6% vs 12.8%, and 292/341 patients (85.6%) in the PIK3CA-mutated cohort had endocrine-resistant disease under stated protocol definitions.

claim_text: Because BYLieve was open-label and noncomparative, it supports activity in a difficult endocrine-resistant setting rather than a definitive comparison against all post-CDK4/6 standards `pmid-39637900`.
evidence_summary: BYLieve cohort A is described as a phase 2 multicenter open-label non-comparative study after CDK4/6 inhibitor plus aromatase inhibitor therapy; it met its activity endpoint and discussion notes nearly all patients were endocrine resistant, while the design precludes definitive comparative claims.
reviewer_notes: Interpretive limitation follows directly from study design.

claim_text: Median investigator-assessed PFS was 15.0 versus 7.3 months, with higher response rate, but the review also notes increased PI3K-class toxicities, few patients with prior adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure, and unresolved questions about sequencing and dose optimization `pmid-40845250`.
corrected_claim: Median investigator-assessed PFS was 15.0 versus 7.3 months, with higher response rate; the FDA summary also reports increased PI3K-class toxicities, few patients with prior adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitor exposure, and a need for dose optimization.
evidence_summary: The FDA approval summary reports INAVO120 investigator-assessed PFS 15.0 vs 7.3 months and ORR 58% vs 25%, describes common PI3K-alpha toxicities and greater patient-reported symptom burden, notes few prior adjuvant CDK4/6 inhibitor-treated patients, and explicitly discusses dose optimization/lower-dose evaluation; it does not clearly frame unresolved sequencing questions as a paper conclusion.
reviewer_notes: Sequencing uncertainty may be a reasonable review-level inference, but the cited paper directly supports the efficacy, toxicity, prior-CDK4/6, and dose-optimization parts.

claim_text: Adding tamoxifen or fulvestrant to PI3K-alpha inhibition reduced viability in resistant cells, inhibited growth of PTEN-null T47D xenografts, and lowered FOXM1, LDHA, and hyperpolarized pyruvate-to-lactate exchange; the authors connect this to convergence of ER and PI3K signaling on FOXM1 `pmid-32976773`.
evidence_summary: ER-positive PIK3CA-mutant models showed acquired or engineered PI3K-alpha inhibitor resistance with persistent FOXM1; combining taselisib/GDC-0032 with tamoxifen or fulvestrant reduced resistant-cell viability, inhibited PTEN KO T47D xenograft growth, lowered FOXM1 and LDHA, and reduced hyperpolarized pyruvate-lactate label exchange.
reviewer_notes: Paper uses taselisib/GDC-0032 prominently, with some alpelisib context.

claim_text: In a phase I/II alpelisib plus aromatase inhibitor study, longitudinal tumor and ctDNA analysis found PTEN loss-of-function mutations in 25 percent of resistant patients and expansion of ESR1 activating mutations associated with resistance `pmid-32864625`.
evidence_summary: The phase I/II alpelisib plus letrozole/exemestane correlative study used longitudinal tumor and plasma ctDNA profiling; it identified PTEN loss-of-function alterations in 25% of resistant patients and found hotspot activating ESR1 mutations increased in number/VAF and were associated with resistance.

claim_text: By contrast, a retrospective SOLAR-1 genomic analysis found that alpelisib plus fulvestrant benefit persisted across several co-alterations previously implicated in endocrine or CDK4/6 inhibitor resistance, including ESR1 and FGFR1 or FGFR2 alterations, while MYC or RAD21 alterations and PTEN alterations were associated with less favorable outcomes or limited benefit signals; the authors caution that subgroup sizes and multiple-testing limits make these hypothesis-generating `pmid-41967638`.
evidence_summary: The retrospective SOLAR-1 NGS analysis reported alpelisib-fulvestrant PFS benefit across several co-alterations including ESR1, and reported benefit in FGFR1/FGFR2 altered subgroups; MYC and RAD21 subgroups had limited PFS benefit, and Cox/multitask models identified PTEN among deleterious PFS factors. The paper states analyses were exploratory, with no multiple-comparison/FDR adjustment and small subgroup caveats.
reviewer_notes: Hypothesis-generating qualifier is supported and important.
